scope: Artifact-only paired statistical analysis of committed MemBud evaluation evidence. No network I/O, no paid model calls, no new model runs, and no changes to existing result artifacts.

method.unit_of_analysis: transition case (one fixed package per case)
method.pairing: Every condition is evaluated on the same frozen cases; paired differences compare the same cases across conditions.

bootstrap.percentile_definition: linear interpolation between order statistics at position (n-1)*q

mcnemar.test: exact two-sided McNemar (binomial sign test on discordant pairs)
mcnemar.p_value: min(1, 2 * P(X <= min(b, c))), X ~ Binomial(b+c, 0.5)

method.per_condition_ci: Wilson score interval (95%) for each binomial rate
method.invalid_input: INVALID_INPUT is a schema-construction failure recorded before verification. Expected-invalid cases are counted in invalid_input_handling and listed as explicit exclusions from paired verifier-decision comparisons; no case is silently dropped.
method.multiplicity: No multiplicity correction: comparisons are descriptive and no confirmatory test is claimed.
method.threshold_tuning: No threshold was selected or tuned on any case from these artifacts.
method.datasets_are_not_pooled: Rules and LLM artifacts differ in verifier construction, and LLM prompt v1 and v2 differ in configuration; each dataset is analyzed separately.

review.limitation: Cases and proposed labels were authored and reviewed by one reviewer (project owner) during milestone development. No second independent human annotation has been collected; scripts/review_cases.py generates a blank second-reviewer sheet and data/review/adjudication-template.md defines the pending process. Treat all labels as exploratory single-reviewer annotations.

rules_artifacts.note: The fairness audit and the evaluation-v2 rules run are independent committed artifacts over the same frozen manifest; their overlapping case decisions match exactly, and the committed graph-vs-text paired differences are reproduced from case rows. They remain separate configurations and are not pooled.

sample_size_rationale.method: Paired-difference precision approximation: 95% CI half-width ~ 1.95996 * sqrt(pi_discordant / n), where pi_discordant is the probability that the two conditions disagree on a paired case. This is a planning approximation, not a power calculation and not a guarantee; McNemar power depends on the split of discordant pairs and the case-level outcomes are not independent draws from a representative population.

current_sample_sizes.statement: The held-out LLM analysis rests on 13 schema-valid cases (7 valid, 6 expected-faulty; 5 expected-invalid are construction failures). The rules analysis rests on 26 non-invalid cases (14 valid, 12 expected-faulty). These are exploratory samples: the intervals are wide, several paired comparisons have zero or two discordant cases, and no result supports a superiority or equivalence claim.

sample_size_rationale.caveat: The table answers 'how wide would the paired-difference interval be at n?' It does not answer 'what n guarantees significance?' and it assumes a discordance rate. No power guarantee is made, and no threshold is selected from this table.

limitations: Labels are single-reviewer exploratory annotations; the second independent human review is pending. Label error is not modelled in these intervals.
Cases are synthetic and were authored alongside the verifiers (circularity risk); they are not a representative benchmark and no population inference is supported.

The v2 LLM prompt was selected using the held-out split; its held-out numbers are development evidence, not a clean independent test. Rules artifacts reuse the dev and held-out splits for descriptive analysis.
Samples are small: 13 schema-valid held-out cases for the LLM analysis and 26 non-invalid rules cases (12 expected-faulty, 14 valid). Several paired comparisons have zero or two discordant cases.
Zero discordance (text_fair vs graph on the rules set; all v2 LLM condition pairs) cannot establish equivalence; the exact test gives p = 1 and the discordance rate is not estimable from the data.
Paired bootstrap intervals resample cases within outcome strata, assume exchangeable cases, and are not corrected for multiplicity or condition selection. Percentile intervals are descriptive.
INVALID_INPUT rows are schema-construction failures, not verifier decisions; they are excluded from paired verifier comparisons and counted separately.
The unguarded condition has no verifier decisions; its APPLIED/ACCEPT rows are a raw-effect baseline, not a verifier outcome.
No superiority, equivalence, or causality claim is made, and no threshold was tuned on these cases.
interpretation: On the committed rules-only evidence, graph and the fair-text control agree on every non-invalid case (26/26); the plain text baseline misses exactly the two constructed contradiction cases, and the paired difference is not statistically distinguishable with 26 non-invalid cases (2 discordant pairs, exact McNemar p = 0.5). The prompt-v2 held-out LLM replay shows all three conditions tied at 7/7 valid accepted and 6/6 expected-faulty detected, but zero discordant pairs cannot support an equivalence claim. The prompt-v1 run is retained as development evidence only. The intervals and the sample-size table show why a fresh, better-powered, independently reviewed evaluation is required before any comparative claim. No superiority or equivalence claim is made for any condition.
